title: Why the China-US Naval Encounter at Sabina Shoal Is Different
gist: China accused the USS Charleston of intruding near Sabina Shoal on October 20; the piece says it is distinct because Sabina Shoal is not China-occupied and the PLA Navy openly admitted tracking a US ship there. The text available is a short excerpt.

insights.claim: On October 20 China's PLA Southern Theater Command Navy said the USS Charleston (LCS-18) illegally intruded near Sabina Shoal in the Spratlys without Chinese approval, while the US 7th Fleet said it conducted routine operations in international waters.
insights.speaker: Bao Yinan
insights.so_what: Fresh South China Sea friction between US and Chinese navies.

insights.claim: Unlike earlier US FONOPs aimed at China, this encounter occurred near a feature China does not occupy, and it was the first time the PLA Navy officially admitted dispatching forces to track a US vessel near such a feature.
insights.speaker: Bao Yinan
insights.so_what: Signals widening Chinese assertion of control beyond occupied features; raises escalation risk for regional shipping.
